_readme: The weekly writer takes the first topic in `queue`, writes it, and moves it to `used`. Add, remove or reorder topics freely. category is development, research or notes. When the queue is empty, the writer proposes its own topic in the next category of the rotation.

queue.title: Zod at the boundaries: making API contracts executable
queue.angle: Why validating data where it enters and leaves a TypeScript app catches drift that types alone miss, with small before/after examples.

queue.title: What CLIP similarity does and does not tell you about a generated image
queue.angle: A practical explainer of CLIP score as an evaluation metric for image generation: what it captures, where it fails, and how to pair it with other checks.

queue.title: Running only the affected tests: fast feedback without skipping safety
queue.angle: How to scope test runs to what changed (Vitest related/changed modes, Playwright tags), and when you still need the full suite.

queue.title: Reading a research paper the way CS197 taught me to
queue.angle: A repeatable method for reading ML papers: first pass, questions, reproducing one figure, and writing down what you still don't believe.

queue.title: LoRA in plain words: what rank 16 actually changes
queue.angle: An intuitive explanation of low-rank adaptation for fine-tuning large models, what the rank controls, and the trade-offs on a single small GPU.

queue.title: Building an Arabic-first interface that doesn't feel translated
queue.angle: Practical RTL and Arabic typography lessons for web apps: logical CSS properties, mirrored icons, numerals, font choice, and testing with real content.

queue.title: Retrieval without a language model: how far can search go?
queue.angle: Classic retrieval (BM25, TF-IDF, good chunking) for answering questions over a long document, and when adding an LLM is actually worth it.

queue.title: Playwright plus axe-core: accessibility checks that run on every pull request
queue.angle: Setting up automated accessibility testing in end-to-end tests, what it catches, and what still needs a human with a keyboard and a screen reader.

queue.title: Why a vision-language model can look at a diagram and still guess
queue.angle: Visual grounding failures in small multimodal models: what they look like, why they happen, and simple ways to probe for them.

queue.title: A decision log for small teams: the cheapest documentation that pays off
queue.angle: What to record in a lightweight decision log, a simple template, and how it helps both humans and AI coding agents stay consistent.

queue.title: Edge detection, learned versus designed
queue.angle: Comparing classic detectors like Canny with learned edge models: what each gets right, and what we give up when edges are learned.

queue.title: Designing a CLI that hands work to AI coding agents safely
queue.angle: What a small Node.js CLI can enforce before an agent starts: fresh branches, acceptance criteria, allowed paths, and a plan step.

queue.title: Speech emotion recognition: what the model hears and what it misses
queue.angle: An introduction to recognising emotion from voice features, common datasets and their limits, and why accuracy numbers can mislead.

queue.title: Learning in chains: following one course into the next
queue.angle: How one bootcamp led to CS229, then CS230, then research methods courses, and how to pick the next thing to learn from the last one.
